newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RAMIREZ DRIVES IN SIX RUNS AS INDIANS CRUSH YANKS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RAMIREZ DRIVES IN SIX RUNS AS INDIANS CRUSH YANKS.

text.p: Manny Ramirez says he feels too much pressure batting cleanup, but he drove in a career-high six runs on four hits Saturday as the Cleveland Indians won at home against the New York Yankees for the first time in 21 months, 13-4.
The win stopped the Indians' seven-game home losing streak to New York and Cleveland avoided becoming the first American League team to lose 1,000 times to one opponent.
The Yankees dropped to 13-3 all-time at Jacobs Field and lost there for the first time since September 1995.
Ramirez, who grew up in the shadows of Yankee Stadium, drilled his 10th homer of the season and his fifth career grand slam well over the left-field wall in the eighth inning for the final margin.
"I like to hit fifth or sixth, I want to hit fifth," said Ramierez, who is 5-for-8 in two games in the cleanup spot.

"I can't take the pressure. I felt a lot of pressure there (batting fourth). I have to stay aggressive in that spot, that's all I can do. (Manager) Mike Hargrove told me that he has a lot of confidence in me and I said, 'Good, okay, let's do it.'"
"People who have a lot of talent have a way of adjusting to things," Hargrove said. "Manny has responded very well in the fourth spot."
Orel Hershiser (7-3) got the win despite surrendering four runs and eight hits in six innings. He is 4-1 with a 3.35 ERA in his last seven starts and is 19-5 all-time at Jacobs Field.

Andy Pettitte (8-5) gave up seven runs -- five earned -- and nine hits with three walks and four strikeouts in 5 1/3 innings. He has struggled recently, going 2-4 with a 4.81 ERA in his last seven starts.
In Toronto, B.J. Surhoff's two-out, two-run single in the eighth rallied the Baltimore Orioles to a 5-1 victory over the Blue Jays.

The rally against Dan Plesac (0-3) spoiled another stellar outing by Roger Clemens, who allowed four hits and two walks with eight strikeouts in seven innings before giving way to the stifling heat after 103 pitches.
Scott Erickson (10-2) gave up a run and six hits with no walks and two strikeouts in seven innings.
Baltimore, which has six two-game losing streaks, is the only major-league team that has not lost three straight.
In Detroit, Tony Clark went 3-for-5 with a home run and a career-high five RBI as the Tigers pounded the Boston Red Sox 15-4.
Damion Easley and Travis Fryman hit back-to-back homers in the second for the Tigers, who matched their season-high in runs scored.
Boston infielder Mike Benjamin became the first position player to pitch in the majors this season when he worked a perfect eighth, getting two fly-outs and a ground-out.
The victory was the third straight for the Tigers. Boston has now lost consecutive games after winning seven-of-eight to crawl out of the American League East basement.
In Texas, Jay Buhner homered and drove in five runs and Joey Cora and Dan Wilson added three RBI apiece as the Seattle Mariners routed the Rangers 15-8.
Mike Maddux (1-0) notched the win despite allowing two runs and four hits in 2 2/3 innings. Greg McCarthy closed the game with 2 1/3 scoreless innings.
Ed Vosberg (1-2) took the loss for Texas, allowing two runs while getting just one batter.
The Mariners have won four of five games from Texas this year.

In Anaheim, Dave Hollins' run-scoring double snapped a seventh-inning tie and an error by Jose Canseco on the play allowed an insurance run to score as the Angels defeated the Oakland Athletics for the sixth straight time, 5-3
Garret Anderson added a two-run triple for the Angels, who improved to 7-1 against division foes this season.
Rich DeLucia (5-2) tossed a scoreless seventh inning to notch the victory. Troy Percival threw a scoreless ninth for his seventh save.
Oakland starter Ariel Prieto (5-5) allowed five runs -- three earned -- and four hits in 6 2/3 innings.

In Chicago, Chris Snopek drove in two runs and James Baldwin (4-8) allowed three runs and four hits over 6 1/3 innings as the White Sox scored a 5-3 victory over the Minnesota Twins, who had a three-game winning streak snapped.
Roberto Hernandez pitched the ninth for his 15th save.
Rich Robertson (7-4) took the loss.
Matt Lawton hit a solo homer for Minnesota.
In Milwaukee, the scheduled game between the Kansas City Royals and Brewers was postponed due to rain. No reschedule date was announced.
